# BarChart

Bar chart: compares values across categories, as grouped or stacked columns, or as horizontal bars. Bars are at
most 24 px thick with a 2 px gap between neighbors and stacked segments; only the data end is rounded.

**Interaction**: each bar is its own hover target and lifts slightly; the tooltip shows its category and value.
`Tab` focuses the chart (focus ring only for the keyboard); `←` / `→` move between categories (`↑` / `↓` with
`orientation="horizontal"`) and `↑` / `↓` between the series of a category (`←` / `→` when horizontal), with
the same tooltip; `Home` / `End` jump to the first and last category and `Esc` hides the tooltip. Legend items
show and hide series without changing colors; the "Chart / Table" switch shows every value as a table.

**Category**: Charts · **Common uses**: Comparing amounts across categories (sales per region), ranked lists (horizontal, largest first), parts
of a total over time (stacked)

## Import

```ts
import { BarChart } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

One series compares a value across categories: every bar has the same color, and the title says what it is.

```tsx
import { BarChart } from 'vellum-ui'

const regions = [
  { region: 'North', orders: 1840, returns: 120 },
  { region: 'South', orders: 1320, returns: 95 },
  { region: 'East', orders: 2210, returns: 160 },
  { region: 'West', orders: 1560, returns: 88 },
  { region: 'Central', orders: 980, returns: 54 },
]

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <BarChart
      title="Orders by region"
      description="Last 30 days"
      data={regions}
      x="region"
      xLabel="Region"
      series={[{ key: 'orders', name: 'Orders' }]}
    />
  )
}
```

## Variants

### Grouped and stacked

Several series are grouped side by side; `stacked` puts them in one bar per category, whose end is the total.
Neighbors are separated by a 2 px gap, and only the data end is rounded.

```tsx
import { BarChart, Stack } from 'vellum-ui'

const quarters = [
  { quarter: 'Q1', hardware: 420, software: 610, services: 280 },
  { quarter: 'Q2', hardware: 455, software: 680, services: 310 },
  { quarter: 'Q3', hardware: 390, software: 720, services: 355 },
  { quarter: 'Q4', hardware: 510, software: 790, services: 402 },
]

export function GroupedAndStacked() {
  const series = [
    { key: 'hardware', name: 'Hardware' },
    { key: 'software', name: 'Software' },
    { key: 'services', name: 'Services' },
  ] as const
  return (
    <Stack gap={4}>
      <BarChart title="Revenue by quarter" data={quarters} x="quarter" series={series} />
      <BarChart
        title="Revenue by quarter, stacked"
        data={quarters}
        x="quarter"
        series={series}
        stacked
        showValues
      />
    </Stack>
  )
}
```

### Horizontal and ranked

`orientation="horizontal"` suits long category names and rankings: sort the rows, largest first. `showValues`
writes each value at the end of its bar.

```tsx
import { BarChart } from 'vellum-ui'

const ranked = [
  { team: 'Platform engineering', tickets: 182 },
  { team: 'Customer success', tickets: 141 },
  { team: 'Design systems', tickets: 96 },
  { team: 'Data and analytics', tickets: 73 },
  { team: 'Security', tickets: 41 },
]

export function Horizontal() {
  return (
    <BarChart
      title="Open tickets by team"
      data={ranked}
      x="team"
      xLabel="Team"
      orientation="horizontal"
      showValues
      series={[{ key: 'tickets', name: 'Open tickets' }]}
    />
  )
}
```

### Negative values

Bars below zero grow down from the baseline and are rounded at their own end.

```tsx
import { BarChart } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Negative() {
  return (
    <BarChart
      title="Change in headcount"
      data={[
        { month: 'Jan', change: 4 },
        { month: 'Feb', change: -2 },
        { month: 'Mar', change: 6 },
        { month: 'Apr', change: -5 },
        { month: 'May', change: 3 },
      ]}
      x="month"
      series={[{ key: 'change', name: 'Change' }]}
      showValues
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `readonly T[]` | The rows: one per category, with a field per series. | — | Yes |
| `x` | `keyof T & string` | Field of the rows that holds the category: on the horizontal axis, or on the vertical axis with `orientation="horizontal"`. | — | Yes |
| `series` | `readonly ChartSeries<keyof T & string>[]` | The series, in legend order. Colors follow the position in this array (or `slot`), so hiding or filtering a series never changes the color of the others. A single series uses one color for every bar. | — | Yes |
| `orientation` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal'` | `vertical`: columns growing up from the horizontal axis; `horizontal`: bars growing right from the vertical axis, better for long category names or many categories. | `'vertical'` | No |
| `stacked` | `boolean` | Stacks the series in one bar per category; the end of the bar is the total. Otherwise the series are grouped side by side. | — | No |
| `showValues` | `boolean` | Writes the value at the end of each bar (the total for stacked bars). Values that do not fit are left out; they stay in the tooltip and the table. | — | No |
| `format` | `ValueFormat` | How values are written on the value axis, at the bar ends, in the tooltip and in the table. | `'auto'` | No |
| `xFormat` | `(value: ChartXValue) => string` | Writes a category, such as a date; by default `String(value)` (dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`). | — | No |
| `xLabel` | `string` | Name of the categories: the header of the first column of the table view. "Category" by default (follows `locale`). | — | No |
| `emphasis` | `keyof T & string` | Key of the one series the chart is about: it keeps its color and the others use the muted color. | — | No |
| `title` | `string` | Title of the chart: what is plotted. It is also the accessible name of the graphic. | — | No |
| `description` | `string` | A short description under the title, such as the period or the unit. | — | No |
| `height` | `number` | Height of the graphic in pixels, axis labels included. The states take the same height. The table view starts at this height and grows with its rows up to 480 px (or this height when it is taller); only longer tables scroll. | `240` | No |
| `loading` | `boolean` | Loading: without data, a delayed loading indicator takes the place of the graphic; with data, the previous graphic stays at reduced opacity until the new data arrives. | — | No |
| `error` | `ReactNode` | Error: `true` shows the default error state; a node is shown as the message of the error state. | — | No |
| `onRetry` | `() => void` | Retry after an error; shows a "Retry" button in the error state. | — | No |
| `emptyDescription` | `ReactNode` | Text of the empty state when there is no data, "No data" by default (follows `locale`). | — | No |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | Actions in the top-right corner, before the view switch (for example a menu or a time range). | — | No |
| `plain` | `boolean` | Without the card (no background, shadow or padding), for charts inside a Panel, a dialog or a drawer. | — | No |

Also accepts `testId` (rendered as `data-testid`), `aria-label`, `role` and `id`, like all primitives.

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.

## Types

Types of this library used above. Import them with `import type { … } from 'vellum-ui'`.

### ChartSeries<K>

A series of a chart.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `K` | Field of the rows that holds the values of this series; also the identity of the series. | — | Yes |
| `name` | `string` | Name of the series in the legend, the tooltip and the table header; shown as text, never interpreted as HTML. | — | Yes |
| `slot` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6 \| 7 \| 8` | Pins the color of the series to a position of the categorical palette (by default its position in the array). | — | No |

### ValueFormat

How a value is written.
- `'auto'`: in full below 10,000, compact from 10,000 on (1,284 · 12.9K · 4.2M).
- `'number'`: always in full, with grouping separators.
- `'compact'`: always compact.
- `'percent'`: the value is a ratio (0.125 → 12.5%).
- a function: your own formatting (units, currencies).

```ts
type ValueFormat = 'auto' | 'number' | 'compact' | 'percent' | ((value: number) => string)
```

### ChartXValue

A value of the category field (x): a text, a number or a date. Dates and numbers are written with `xFormat`
(otherwise as `String(value)`).

```ts
type ChartXValue = string | number | Date
```
